Our story

36 years of owner-present construction

RKM Homes was founded in 1987 by Kerry Moore to prove that a small budget doesn't mean cheap construction. Family and veteran owned, the business now operates under Kerry's son-in-law Keith, preserving 36 years of design expertise and client relationships. Kerry draws every home himself and is present on every job site—a hands-on approach that limits RKM to a handful of projects per year. Every client receives fixed-price agreements, in-house warranty management, and professional interior design support for selections.

Good to know

Questions, answered.

How does RKM keep costs down without cutting quality?

Kerry draws plans in-house, eliminating architectural firm markups. Fixed-price agreements prevent scope creep. RKM's financial strength allows cash-flowing projects and paying suppliers within 7–10 days, which keeps subcontractors responsive and timelines on track. You only go over budget if you request changes to the original specifications.

What's included in the fixed-price agreement?

The contract covers the entire project with realistic allowances for interior finishes. RKM provides a detailed budget and spec sheet upfront. All changes are quoted for approval and tracked throughout construction so you always know where you stand financially.

Can RKM work with my own interior designer?

Yes. RKM's interior design services are optional. If you already have a designer, RKM is happy to coordinate with them instead.

How many homes does RKM build per year?

RKM builds only a handful of homes per year because Kerry is present on every job site and involved in every decision. This limited volume ensures personal attention and quality oversight.

What areas does RKM serve?

RKM builds throughout the Front Range, including Elbert, Douglas, and Arapahoe counties. Communities include Elizabeth, Larkspur, Castle Rock, Lone Tree, Aurora, Littleton, Centennial, Englewood, and surrounding areas.

Does RKM handle warranty claims?

Yes. RKM manages all warranty work in-house, so you don't work with a third-party provider for repairs.
